name: Creators Toolbox
tagline: A bundled set of small utilities for content creators: idea and caption help, content planning, and repurposing busywork.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Bundled creator toolboxes are usually a dozen thin utilities wrapped in one subscription, and thin utilities are exactly what coding agents are good at. A local version that generates hooks and captions, holds an idea bank, and keeps a content calendar is a single session of work with an LLM key in .env. The gaps show up the moment a tool needs to touch a platform: posting, scheduling, pulling your own analytics, or reading trending data all mean OAuth apps, review processes, and rate limits. Without knowing exactly which tools are inside this particular bundle, assume the text and planning half is trivially replaceable and the platform-connected half is a weekend of API paperwork you will resent. Build it if you use three of the tools; keep paying if you use fifteen.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app that turns a topic or long script into hooks, captions, and short-form cuts, then files them in an idea bank and a simple content calendar.
requirements: An LLM API key (OpenAI or Anthropic) in .env
Platform developer apps and OAuth if you want actual publishing, which the base build skips
whatYouLose: Any tool in the bundle you did not think to rebuild, which is usually the one you end up needing
Real publishing and scheduling into platforms, plus the maintenance when their APIs change
Trend or benchmark data the vendor aggregates across users
Mobile access unless you host it somewhere and add auth
Someone else keeping prompts and templates current as models and platform formats move
moatNotes: The moat here is breadth and upkeep, not technology: one person rebuilds three tools, the vendor maintains thirty.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the value of a toolbox is that it is already there. Rebuilding the two tools you use weekly is a fun Saturday, but creators pay so that the fifteenth odd job, a thumbnail resize, a hashtag set, a repurposing template, is a click instead of another prompt session. Add publishing integrations and the calculus tips further: nobody wants to maintain OAuth tokens for four platforms as a hobby.
notes: Grab-bag products are replaceable one tool at a time, which is also why people keep paying for the bag.
prompt:
Build a local-only "creator toolbox" web app in an empty folder. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Next.js (App Router, TypeScript) with Tailwind.
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/toolbox.db, schema created on first run.
- One LLM provider: OpenAI, key read from process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY. Write .env.example, never commit .env.

Features, all in one sidebar layout:
1. Hook and caption generator: paste a topic or rough note, pick a platform (shorts, reels, tiktok, x, linkedin, youtube long), get 10 hooks and 3 caption variants with a character count per platform limit. One click copy, one click save to Idea Bank.
2. Repurposer: paste a long transcript or script, return 5 short-form segments with a suggested timestamp range, a hook, and an on-screen text overlay line.
3. Idea Bank: saved items in SQLite, each with status (idea, drafting, scheduled, posted), platform tag, and free text notes. Full-text search over title and body.
4. Content calendar: month grid, drag an Idea Bank item onto a date to set a planned date. Stored locally. Read-only iCal export at /api/calendar.ics.
5. Prompt templates: editable templates stored in the DB, used by features 1 and 2, so the user can tune voice without touching code. Ship 6 sensible defaults.

Explicitly out of scope: publishing or scheduling to any platform, OAuth, platform analytics, trending data, image or video generation, multi-user auth, payments.

Quality bar: every LLM call streams, has a visible loading state, and fails with a readable error instead of a blank screen. Seed the DB with 3 example ideas. Include a README with setup in under 5 commands and a one-paragraph note on what this deliberately does not do.
